competitive_landscape: The river is served today by the Saigon Waterbus (commuter/tourist) and, on the Vung Tau corridor, by Greenlines DP fast diesel catamarans that replaced the retired Soviet-era hydrofoils. Demand is proven and growing, but the experience is slow, diesel and weather-and-tide exposed. There is no foiling incumbent — the opportunity is to be the clean, fast, reliable tier the existing operators can't deliver.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The urban river-transit spine — Bach Dang↔Thu Thiem↔Thanh Da↔Thu Duc (all <10 nm) — sits comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope with terminal charging between runs, supporting high-frequency commuter rotations.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta-LR's 700 nm hybrid range covers the Vung Tau line-haul (~60 nm), Can Gio (~30 nm) and the Mekong-Delta gateway (~40 nm) with no charging-infrastructure dependency at the suburban, beach or delta ends.

precedents.why_it_matters: Demonstrates electric foiling as the backbone of inter-island mobility at national scale — the proof that a foiling fleet can be the transport layer, not a novelty.

regulatory_note: Vinamarine + HCMC Department of Transport license inland-waterway passenger routes (the Saigon Waterbus is the established template); Vietnam Inland Waterways Administration for the river segments; Ba Ria–Vung Tau Province at the Vung Tau end; Can Gio biosphere overlay on the SE arm.
seasonality: Dec–Apr (dry season) is calmest on the river and the Vung Tau crossing; May–Nov brings monsoon downpours and post-storm river debris. The basin sits largely outside the main typhoon track — a relatively benign year-round operating environment.

summary: Ho Chi Minh City is Vietnam's economic capital and one of Southeast Asia's most congested megacities, bisected by the Saigon River and ringed by rivers and canals. The Saigon Waterbus (launched 2017) and the historic Saigon↔Vung Tau hydrofoil corridor both proved latent water-transit demand, yet the river carries a tiny share of trips. The opportunity is three layers: a silent zero-wake commuter spine along the Saigon River (Bach Dang↔Thu Thiem↔Thu Duc), a flagship line-haul reviving the ~60 nm Vung Tau corridor, and links to the Can Gio biosphere mega-project and the Mekong Delta. As Grab's strongest commuter market in Vietnam, an in-app foiling river-transit tier is exactly the congestion-beating overlay the platform monetizes.
tagline: A 9-million-person megacity with legendary gridlock, a big river running through it, and a water-bus that already proved the demand — the river is the city's most under-used highway.

use_cases.body: A silent zero-wake foiling river-bus from Bach Dang to Thu Thiem, Thanh Da and Thu Duc — turning the river into the real commuter highway the Waterbus only hinted at.
